key_insight: An LLM-guided workflow redesigned a magnesium stent across about 1,650 CAD parameters, reducing a high-percentile bend-strain objective by 32% within 15 nonlinear simulations.
engineering_relevance: The approach could enable coordinated component redesign when high-dimensional CAD models and costly nonlinear finite-element solves limit conventional optimisation.
method: GPT-6 Astra proposed coordinated edits to the stent’s CAD parameters.
Each proposal was built, meshed and evaluated with large-deformation plasticity and contact.
The LLM used full simulation results to guide subsequent designs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 32% objective reduction versus roughly 10% for Tosca at the same simulation budget; an earlier LLM design independently evaluated through full deployment showed 14% lower strain and 63% less damage at its most damaged spot.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to one component study, and the final 32%-improved design was not the design checked in the independent higher-fidelity deployment model.
paper_title: AI agents can redesign engineering parts with more than a thousand CAD parameters and nonlinear simulations
